"''This armor is part of our identity. It makes us Mandalorians who we are.|Sabine and [[Alrich Wren]]|}} '''Mandalorian armor''', known as '''''beskar'gam''''' in [[Mando'a]], referred to the traditional [[armor]] worn by the warrior clans of the planet [[Mandalore]]. Common traits included a helmet with a T-shaped visor, called a [[macrobinocular viewplate]], that concealed their faces, and armaments like [[Mandalorian vambrace|vambraces]] and [[jetpack]]s. The [[Mandalorian]]s' bloody history made their armor an iconic symbol of fear. Mandalorian armor was typically made from [[beskar]], which was one of the strongest [[metal]]s in the galaxy, but it could also be made from more common metals such as [[durasteel]]. Beskar could protect the wearer from [[blaster]]s and even [[lightsaber]]s. The famed Mandalorian [[bounty hunter]] and [[foundling]] [[Jango Fett]] wore [[Boba Fett's armor|customized armor]] made of beskar alloy, which was later inherited by his cloned son [[Boba Fett|Boba]]. The [[Arc Pulse Generator]], an [[Galactic Empire|Imperial]] [[superweapon]], was capable of superheating the beskar alloy used in Mandalorian armor to incinerate its wearer. ==Description== ===Overview=== {{Quote|With right calibration, a blaster could pass right through Mandalorian armor.''"
"''Impossible. You try that, a Mandalorian would break you in two.''"
"''Funny, that's exactly how the guy who told me died.|Two stormtroopers converse five years into the Imperial Era|''[[Star Wars Jedi: Fallen Order]]''}} [[File:Chapter2-Din-working.png|thumb|left|300px|Din Djarin repairing his damaged armor]] Generally the [[armor]] was made from [[beskar]], a highly durable [[metal]] which could repel [[blaster]] fire''[[Star Wars: The Mandalorian]]'' and [[lightsaber]] strikes.''[[Ultimate Star Wars, New Edition]]'' In order to pierce Mandalorian armor, a weapon made of pure beskar such as a [[beskar spear]] would be required.{{Databank|beskar-spear|Beskar spear}} Identified as a [[macrobinocular viewplate]], the helmets had an angled visor.''[[Star Wars Rebels: The Visual Guide]]'' Due to the durability of the beskar metal, some armor sets were hundreds of years old, such as in the case of [[Sabine Wren]]'s armor. Beskar armor was forged by [[Mandalorian Armorer]]s.{{Databank|the-armorer|the Armorer}} The Mandalorian method for forging beskar was a closely guarded secret, a skill passed on through generations to keep ancient armor intact and impervious.{{Databank|the-armorer-s-forge|The Armorer's forge}} ===Design=== {{Quote|My armor is like my second skin. I'm being serious: sometimes I totally forget I even have it on and I fall asleep in it.|Sabine Wren|}} Traditional Mandalorian armor consisted of a helmet, shoulder [[pauldron]]s, vambraces, breastplate, codpiece, kneepads, and thigh and shin guards clasped over a body stocking. Most Mandalorians painted their armor, though some, such as Din Djarin, did not paint their pure beskar pieces. Mandalorian helmets often had a [[macrobinocular viewplate]], tactical [[heads-up display]]s,''[[Star Wars: Absolutely Everything You Need to Know]]'' a [[comlink]], and an [[antenna]] tipped with a [[rangefinder]] that could be pulled over the viewplate to enhance imagery. Mandalorians also wore [[magnet]]ized [[boot]]s. Sabine Wren programmed a [[holo-imager]] in [[Sabine Wren's modified Nite Owl helmet|her helmet's]] rangefinder to take snapshots. [[File:JangoFett-SWBC7-20.png|thumb|right|250px|A complete set of Mandalorian armor worn by Jango Fett]] The [[Ka'rta]] symbol{{BuildFalconCite|32|Guide to the Galaxy}} was featured on the chest plate of the armor.{{Film|II}} [[Mandalorian vambrace]]s were [[computer]]-controlled tools bristling with [[weapon]]ry, designed to combat the [[Force power|Force abilities]] of a [[Jedi]].{{Databank|mandalorian-vambraces|Mandalorian Vambraces}} They potentially included: *[[Wrist blaster|Blasters]] *[[Dart]]s **[[Electroshock dart]]s{{TheMandalorian|Chapter 22: Guns for Hire}} **[[Paralyzing dart]]s **[[Poison dart]]s ***[[Kamino saberdart]]s *[[Flamethrower]]s{{TCW|Shades of Reason}} *[[Grappling line]]s{{Rebels|Trials of the Darksaber}} *[[Dur-24 wrist laser|Lasers]] *[[Projectile buzzsaw]]s *[[Repulsorlift|Repulsors]] *[[Missile|Rockets]] *[[Personal Combat Shield|Shield projectors]] *[[Vibroblade]]s{{TheMandalorian|Chapter 11: The Heiress}} *[[Whipcord launcher|Whipcords]] *[[Whistling bird]]s{{TheMandalorian|Chapter 3: The Sin}} The Mandalorians used many models of [[jetpack]]s, including the [[Z-6 jetpack|Z-6]] and [[JT-12 jetpack|JT-12]], to increase maneuverability in combat as well as fly. These were often tipped with a launcher that were used to fire anti-vehicle [[Missile|homing missiles]]. However, they could also be used to fire a [[grappling hook]] linked to an internal winch. [[Gyro stabilizer|Gyro-stabilizer]]s made it easy to maneuver in the air, and were capable of both short jumps and long-distance flight. ===Variant armor types=== *[[Heavy Infantry Mandalorian Armor]] *[[Imperial Super Commando armor]] *[[Mandalorian rally master armor]] ==History== ===Tradition of Mandalore=== [[File:TCW_Neo-Crusader_helmet.png|thumb|left|200px|A Neo-Crusader's helmet]] The ancient [[Mandalorian crusaders]] wore [[Armor|helmets]] over [[cloak]]s.{{SW|url=series/clone-wars/shades-of-reason-trivia-gallery|text="Shades of Reason" Trivia Gallery}} {{C|Slides 3 and 4}} The [[Mandalorian Neo-Crusaders]] also wore helmets.{{TCW|Wookiee Hunt}} After encountering the Jedi during the early [[Mandalorian crusades|crusades]], the [[Mandalorian-Jedi War]] began, and it was during this period that the Mandalorians created their signature armor, weaponry and fighting style in order to combat the [[Jedi Knight]]s and their [[The Force|Force]] abilities.{{WebCite|url=http://comicbook.com/starwars/2017/02/18/star-wars-rebels-knights-of-the-old-republic-reference-confirmed|text=Star Wars Rebels Showrunner Explains Major Knight of the Old Republic Reference|author=Lucas Siegel|archivedate=20170220002112}} During the time after the [[Great Clan Wars|Mandalorian Civil War]], two styles of Mandalorian armor would emerge—the formidable traditional armor of the warrior clans like [[Death Watch]], and those of the pacifist [[New Mandalorians]]. Death Watch's [[Gender|female]] warriors, the [[Nite Owls]], wore a different set of armor.{{TCW|A Friend in Need}} The famed Mandalorian [[bounty hunter]][[War of the Bounty Hunters – IG-88 1|''War of the Bounty Hunters – IG-88'' 1]] and [[foundling]]{{TheMandalorian|Chapter 14: The Tragedy}} [[Jango Fett]] wore the [[Boba Fett's armor|armor]] type, which had been given to him during the [[Mandalorian Civil Wars]]{{BustCollectionCite|20|Character}} by the Mandalorians.{{TheMandalorian|Chapter 14: The Tragedy}} [[Prime Minister]] [[Almec]], however, expressed bewilderment as to how he would have obtained it, decrying Fett as nothing but a common [[bounty hunter]]. The [[Kaminoan]]s who [[Cloning|cloned]] him to create the [[Grand Army of the Republic]] took inspiration from his suit for the [[clone trooper armor]]. ===Clone Wars=== [[File:MandalorianArmor-USWNE.png|thumb|right|250px|A Mandalorian member of Death Watch armed with a [[GALAAR-15 blaster carbine]]]] After Fett was [[Death|killed]] by [[Jedi Master]] [[Mace Windu]] during the [[First Battle of Geonosis]], his helmet was used by [[Boba Fett|Boba]] as a bomb in an [[Mission to Vanqor|attempt]] on Windu's life.{{TCW|R2 Come Home}} By the [[Imperial Era|Age of the Empire]], Boba had inherited his father's armor and rebuilt it in his memory.''[[Star Wars: The Complete Visual Dictionary, New Edition]]'' When the renegade [[Sith Lord]] [[Maul]] defeated and killed [[Pre Vizsla]] and became ruler of Mandalore during the [[Clone Wars]], his followers in Death Watch customized their armor with painted helmets, handprints, and horns resembling their new [[Dathomirian]] [[Zabrak]] leader, becoming [[Mandalorian super commando]]s. A large number of them had clawed handprints over their helmets, similar to{{TCW|The Lawless}} the handprint of [[Rishi eel]] [[blood]] on [[clone trooper]] [[Echo]]'s chestplate.{{TCW|Rookies (episode)}} The [[Journeyman Protector|Mandalorian Protectors]], such as the those who served with [[Fenn Rau]] in [[Skull Squadron]], wore armor when they fought at the [[Third Battle of Mygeeto|Third Battle]] of [[Mygeeto]].[[Kanan 10|''Kanan'' 10]] ===Age of the Empire=== {{Quote|A Mandalorian without armor is no more than a common soldier.|[[Tiber Saxon]]|}} [[File:BobaFett-Db.png|thumb|left|250px|Boba Fett, wearing his Mandalorian armor]] Following the end of the Clone Wars, the Protectors continued to wear the armor as part of their arrangement with the [[Galactic Empire]] at their [[Protectors Camp|encampment]] on [[Concord Dawn]]'s [[Third moon of Concord Dawn|third moon]].{{Rebels|The Protector of Concord Dawn}} [[Soldier]]s throughout the [[Imperial Military]] took note of the armor's durability, leading one intrepid [[stormtrooper]] to develop a hypothesis that a finely-calibrated blaster could pierce it. His experiment ended in failure, however, when he tested his theory on a Mandalorian warrior, who promptly broke the stormtrooper in two. [[Gar Saxon]], acting as the Imperial [[Viceroy]] of Mandalore, along with [[Imperial Super Commando]]s such as [[Tristan Wren]],{{Rebels|Legacy of Mandalore}} wore armor that resembled stormtrooper [[Stormtrooper armor|armor]].{{Rebels|Imperial Supercommandos}} Members of [[Clan Wren]], such as its leader, [[Countess]] [[Ursa Wren]], wore armor with yellow markings. [[Sabine Wren]] wore a [[Sabine Wren's armor|suit of Mandalorian armor]] that dated back to circa [[500 BBY]],''[[Star Wars: Timelines]]'' {{C|bonus content}} reforging it to her liking and regularly repainting it. She wore the armor as part of the [[Spectres]] rebel cell and throughout the [[Mandalorian Civil War (Imperial Era)|Mandalorian Civil War]] that ended in the overthrow of Clan Saxon. In the [[Liberation of Lothal|liberation]] of the planet [[Lothal]], Wren was unable to save her close friend, [[Ezra Bridger]], from exiling himself, the Imperial [[Grand Admiral]] [[Mitth'raw'nuruodo]], and the crew of [[Star Destroyer]] ''[[Chimaera]]''{{Rebels|Family Reunion – and Farewell}} into [[Far galaxy|another galaxy]]{{Ahsoka|Part Two: Toil and Trouble}} to save Lothal. Wren stayed on Lothal''[[Ultimate Star Wars, New Edition]]'' in order to keep it safe in Bridger's absence. At some point during his bounty hunting career, Boba Fett began to wear his father's Mandalorian armor.''[[Star Wars: The Complete Visual Dictionary, New Edition]]'' Sometime after the [[Battle of Endor]], Fett's set of Mandalorian armor ended up in storage in a [[Jawa]] [[sandcrawler]] on [[Tatooine]]. [[Cobb Vanth]], who was on the sandcrawler after the Jawas rescued him from dehydration in the desert, happened upon a crate containing the armor. After trading valuable [[Silicax oxalate|silicax crystals]] with the Jawas, he attained the armor for his own, and wore it to defend the town of [[Freetown|Mos Pelgo]].{{TheMandalorian|Chapter 9: The Marshal}} The [[pirate]] [[Kars Tal-Korla]] wore a trademark suit of patchwork armor made from [[Corellian]], Imperial trooper, and Mandalorian.[[Aftermath (novel)|''Aftermath'']] ===New Republic Era=== ====Surviving the Great Purge==== [[File:Paz-Vizsla-AG.png|thumb|right|220px|Paz Vizsla wore a suit of blue heavy infantry armor.]] During the [[New Republic Era]], the Mandalorians became rarer to see, after the [[Great Purge of Mandalore]] by the Empire against them. During that time, the Empire also plundered vast amounts of Beskar from the Mandalorians. The Mandalorians took orphans in as foundlings. One Mandalorian [[The Tribe|tribe]] of the [[Children of the Watch]], who preached that a Mandalorian was never to remove their helmet in the presence of others,{{TheMandalorian|Chapter 11: The Heiress}} hid in an [[The Enclave|enclave]] under [[Nevarro City]] on the [[planet]] [[Nevarro]]. However, after they [[Clash on Nevarro|fought]] the [[Bounty Hunters' Guild]] in the city, an [[Gideon's Imperial remnant|Imperial remnant]] cracked down on them, [[Attack on the Tribe|killing]] many. Their armor was piled up in the enclave to be salvaged by [[the Armorer]], one of the few survivors from the tribe. Another survivor, bounty hunter [[Din Djarin]], was given a [[signet]] depicting a [[mudhorn]] on [[Din Djarin's armor|his armor]] to symbolize the [[Clan Mudhorn|clan]] consisting of himself and [[Din Grogu|Grogu]].{{TheMandalorian|Chapter 8: Redemption}} Seeking out other Mandalorians to help in his quest to bring Grogu to the Jedi, Djarin [[Mission to Tatooine (Din Djarin)|arrived]] in the town of Mos Pelgo on Tatooine. There, he encountered Cobb Vanth, who was still wearing Boba Fett's armor to defend the town. As Djarin did not want a non-Mandalorian to wear it, Vanth agreed to give over the armor if the bounty hunter helped kill a [[leviathan krayt dragon]] that had been terrorizing his town. After the creature's death, Vanth stayed true to his word and gave over the armor, parting on good terms with Djarin. Unknown to the bounty hunter, as he left the town, he was being watched by the still-alive Fett. After successfully helping a [[Frog Lady|passenger]] and her eggs reach [[Trask]] and reunite with her [[Frog Man|husband]], Djarin was recruited by [[Bo-Katan Kryze]], [[Axe Woves]], and [[Koska Reeves]] to help them raid a [[Imperial Gozanti-class cruiser|''Gozanti''-class cruiser]] belonging to the remnant in order to capture some weapons being exported from the black market port. Although Djarin was disturbed that they removed their helmets and learned his beliefs were not held by all Mandalorians, the quartet of [[Mandalorian]]s fought through several units of [[stormtrooper]]s to reach the cargo hold. The quartet were temporarily stopped by a remnant officer who trapped them in the cargo control area. The officer, and a group of stormtroopers that accompanied him in defending the hold were jettisoned. After Kryze revealed to the [[Unidentified Imperial captain|captain]] that he had captured the cargo hold, the captain stated that even if they jettisoned the crates of cargo, they would comb the area and kill them. Kryze revealed that her true objective was to fully capture the ship and storm the [[Bridge (starship)|bridge]] even to the distraught and shock of Djarin. Djarin eventually agreed to help Kryze storm the bridge and fully capture the ship, in return Kyrze would reveal the whereabouts of a [[Ahsoka Tano|Jedi]]. ====The adventures of Fett and Djarin==== Djarin and Boba Fett would come face-to-face on [[Tython]], when Fett would employ the skills of sharpshooter [[Fennec Shand]], whom Fett had saved on Tatooine. Shand, having Grogu in her sights, would stand down and in exchange Djarin would remove his jetpack. Fett would then demand his armor be returned to him, having tracked it and the Mandalorian to the inner core planet. Djarin refused, believing the armor was looted in the [[Great Purge of Mandalore]] and belonged to the Mandalorian people. Fett would argue, however, that the armor had in fact been passed down to him from his father, who had been gifted it by one of Djarin's forebearers. The arrival of Imperial remnants would cut the conversation short, with Fett offering to trade the return of his armor in exchange for guaranteeing both Grogu and Djarin's safety. [[File:BobaCleansUpGood-TMCh15.png|thumb|left|300px|Din Djarin and Boba Fett on Morak.]] During the ensuing conflict, Fett would take his armor from Djarin's ''[[Razor Crest]]'', while Shand and Djarin continued to fight the reinforced Imperial remnants. Late into the skirmish, Djarin and Shand would find themselves surrounded, outmanned, and outgunned. Djarin would use his beskar-clad body to prevent Shand from being hit by Imperial blaster fire, while the two returned fire. Fett would drop two explosives on the battlefield from above, then display its capabilities by singlehandedly eliminating an entire platoon of stormtroopers, as well as two [[Imperial Troop Transport|Imperial troop dropships]]. Fett utilized an array of offensive weapons including a [[Dur-24 wrist laser|wrist laser]], [[MM9 mini concussion rocket launcher|concussion rockets]], [[Kneepad rocket dart launcher|kneepad rocket darts]], and a jetpack-launched missile. Afterward, Fett would show Djarin his [[chain code]], which proved that the ownership of the armor had indeed been that of a Mandalorian foundling; Boba's father, Jango Fett. Pledging to assist the Mandalorian in Grogu's rescue as part of their deal, Fett, Djarin, and Shand would depart for Navarro on ''[[Slave I]]''. Djarin and Fett joined forces with Kryze and Reeves for the [[second rescue of Grogu]], during which Djarin removed his helmet to say goodbye to Grogu when Jedi Knight [[Luke Skywalker]] arrived to train the Child.{{TheMandalorian|Chapter 16: The Rescue}} Fighting side-by-side, Fett and Djarin later used their armor to defend themselves against [[Pyke Syndicate Foot Soldier|Pyke guards]] during the [[Battle of Mos Espa]], during which Grogu also reunited with Djarin.{{BOBF|Chapter 7: In the Name of Honor}} ====The return to Mandalore==== [[File:BoKatanKryze-Platinum2023.png|thumb|right|200px|Bo-Katan Kryze was Mand'alor during the New Republic Era.]] [[The Armorer]] continued to make armor for her [[Mandalorian secret covert|Mandalorian covert]], including children such as [[Ragnar Vizsla]].{{TheMandalorian|Chapter 17: The Apostate}} Having removed his helmet in the presence of others during Grogu's rescue, Djarin made his way to the ruins of Mandalore to bathe in the [[Living Waters]] and be redeemed in the eyes of the Children of the Watch.{{TheMandalorian|Chapter 18: The Mines of Mandalore}} For the mission, he was joined by Kryze, whose forces had abandoned her when she failed to secure the Darksaber. Kryze dove into the waters after Djarin fell in, where she discovered a surviving [[Mythosaur]] and, by virtue of entering the waters and then not removing her helmet in the presence of others afterward, was, too, redeemed in the eyes of the Tribe. Both Djarin and Kryze were welcomed into the covert.{{TheMandalorian|Chapter 19: The Convert}} Shortly into her stay, she led the [[rescue of Ragnar Vizsla]] and lost one of her pauldrons. Thus, she was given a new, silver replacement by the Armorer, who also provided Grogu with a roundel.{{TheMandalorian|Chapter 20: The Foundling}} After the Mandalorian Tribe arrived to Nevarro and freed the world from a [[Pirate siege on Nevarro|pirate siege]], the Armorer decreed that Kryze was welcome to walk both worlds: she could be both a Mandalorian who removed her helmet and be considered part of the Children of the Watch.{{TheMandalorian|Chapter 21: The Pirate}} With Kryze regaining the loyalty of her forces when they discovered she had reclaimed the Darksaber,{{TheMandalorian|Chapter 22: Guns for Hire}} the assembled ranks of traditionalist and non-traditionalist Mandalorians ventured to Mandalore and [[Liberation of Mandalore|reconquered the world]] from Gideon. In the battle, Gideon wore a suit of [[Dark Trooper phase 4|beskar Dark Trooper armor]] and commanded a force [[Imperial armored commando armor|beskar-wearing]] [[Imperial armored commando]]s, but the Imperials would be defeated. Together, Kryze's followers and the Children of the Watch reignited the [[Great Forge]].{{TheMandalorian|Chapter 24: The Return}} ====New days for all==== While the reunited Mandalorian people made a life for themselves on their reclaimed homeworld, Djarin and Grogu would make their way back to Nevarro, where the Mandalorians had already been granted land to call home by Karga in addition to Mandalore. In another gift from Karga, Djarin and Grogu were also given a [[Clan Mudhorn cabin|cabin]] outside of [[Nevarro City]], where Djarin relaxed in his armor as Grogu practiced his Force powers. Meanwhile, Wren continued to make a life for herself on Lothal, where she kept her armor hidden within Bridger's old [[LothalNet comm tower E-272|comm tower roost]]. As the [[quest to find Ezra Bridger]] resumed, she unearthed and redonned her armor,{{Ahsoka|Part Two: Toil and Trouble}} using it throughout the [[incident on Seatos]]{{Ahsoka|Part Four: Fallen Jedi}} and the [[Mission on Peridea|battles]] on the extragalactic [[Peridea]]. While Bridger was [[Battle of Peridea|ultimately able to escape]] back home aboard the Star Destroyer ''Chimaera'', Wren, still donning her armor, was left behind on Peridea with her Jedi mentor [[Ahsoka Tano]].{{Ahsoka|Part Eight: The Jedi, the Witch, and the Warlord}} ==Behind the scenes== During production of [[The Mandalorian Season Three|''The Mandalorian'' Season Three]], [[Dave Filoni]], [[Rick Famuyiwa]], and [[Jon Favreau]] wanted an audio sound that signaled to the audience Mandalorians could pressurize their helmets, thereby keeping them safe for treks into possibly toxic areas. Given "a very specific note" to show as such, sound designer [[David W. Collins]] used the iconic squeak of Vader's helmet sealing over his head in "[[Chapter 17: The Apostate]]" for when Ragnar put on his helmet.{{InsiderCite|221|Turn It Up!}} ==Appearances==
